question: When performing a mediolateral episiotomy, the recommended angle of incision from the midline at the time of cutting is:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An incision at 15–20 degrees is nearly midline and has a high risk of extending into the anal sphincter complex, particularly during delivery.
While 30–35 degrees is more lateral than a midline cut, it still underestimates the perineal tissue shift during crowning. The recommended angle at the time of cutting is greater.

Correct. The recommended angle at the time of cutting is 60 degrees from the midline (away from the anus). As the perineum stretches during delivery, this results in the actual healed scar lying at approximately 40–45 degrees — the desired position that avoids the anal sphincter.

answers.text: 90 degrees from the midline, i.e., a purely lateral incision

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A purely lateral incision (90 degrees) risks entering the lateral perineal structures, ischioanal fossa, and pudendal vessels, and is technically much more difficult to repair.

overallFeedback.feedback: The recommended cutting angle for mediolateral episiotomy is 60 degrees from the midline at the time of incision. Perineal stretch during crowning moves the scar medially, so cutting at 60 degrees achieves the desired 40–45 degree healed position.
Correct. Cut at 60 degrees from the midline — the perineum moves medially during crowning, so the final scar position is approximately 40–45 degrees, which is the safe mediolateral position.
